rejected.title: Stopping the plugin only clears the interval; dispatcher passes already running keep messaging and writing
rejected.why:
The finding depends on the old and new plugin instances running at the same time during `paseo plugin reload`, with two BoardStores writing board.json. The Paseo daemon (read-only grep of /Applications/Paseo.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar) never lets that happen:

1. Each user plugin runs in its own forked child process: `spawnPluginChild()` calls `fork(worker, [], { serialization: "advanced", stdio: [..., "ipc"] })`. Only built-ins use InternalPluginChild. So the old instance's AutomationService, BoardStore and timers live in a process of their own.

2. `reloadPlugin(pluginId)` runs `await this.stopPlugin(pluginId); await this.startExplicit(...)` inside a serialized `enqueue`. `stopPlugin` calls `runtime.stopPluginById`, which sends `{type:"shutdown"}` and then waits on the child's `close` event. A force timer sends SIGTERM after SOFT_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000 and SIGKILL 2 s after that. The new process starts only after the old one has exited, so the two instances never overlap.

3. Inside the child, `shutdown()` does three things before or around the plugin cleanup: it calls `paseo.dispose()`, which disables the Paseo connection the finding says the old instance "kept"; it calls `hooks.close()`, so no new hook handlers start; and it sets `stopping`, so later requests are rejected. After the cleanup it closes the daemon client and disconnects the channel.

So step 2 of the failure scenario ("the new instance's first attach runs reconcile on the same turn end" while the old instance is still in its pass) cannot happen. Both instances can't load board.json before either writes, and the agent can't get two nudges from two instances. A pass the old process is killed in the middle of can't tear board.json either: BoardStore writes a temp file and renames it, and pendingOp/`starting` are recorded before side effects so the next instance resumes them. The new instance's reconcile then handles any turn end the old one didn't record, guarded by `turnAt`.

What does survive, and is not what was reported: a pass already awaiting inside the old process during the at most ~2 s shutdown window can see its `paseo...send()`/`create()` fail because the API was disposed. `sideEffectFailed` then commits a spurious `retry_wait`/`start_failed` with failures+1, or closes the job as failed if failureLimit is reached. That is a minor robustness issue that a full daemon shutdown triggers too, and a `stopped` flag checked only at `kick()` entry wouldn't fix it. The real fix would be to skip `sideEffectFailed` once stopped. The concurrency/double-write bug as reported is refuted. | The finding depends on the old and new plugin instances running at the same time, each with its own BoardStore writing the same board.json. The Paseo daemon does not allow that for a plugin like Flowly. I checked the daemon's plugin runtime inside /Applications/Paseo.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar:

- A plugin that is not built in runs in its own forked child process (`spawnPluginChild` calls `fork(plugin-process.js)`). Only built-in plugins use the in-process `InternalPluginChild`. The daemon runs Flowly from a local git ref, so Flowly gets a child process.
- `reloadPlugin` first runs `await this.stopPlugin(pluginId)` and only then `await this.startExplicit(...)`.
- `stopPlugin` sends `shutdown` and waits for the child's `close` event. After SOFT_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000 it sends SIGTERM, and 2 s later SIGKILL. Only then does it resolve.
- On the child side, `shutdown()` runs in this order: sets `stopping = true` (new requests are rejected), `paseo.dispose()`, `hooks.close()` (no more hook deliveries), the plugin cleanup (`automation.stop()`), closes the daemon client, then `channel.disconnect()`.

So the new instance's first `attach` and reconcile can only start after the old process has exited. The two stores never interleave load-modify-write, and the double-nudge or lost-write scenario cannot happen. A full daemon restart likewise stops the children first.

What remains is a pass that was already running when shutdown began. It can do at most a few seconds of extra work before the process dies, and none of it overlaps the new instance. Its Paseo calls fail once `dispose()` has run. A write cut off by SIGKILL is harmless because the store writes to a temp file and renames it. A commit-then-side-effect step cut off at the kill is the crash case the design already covers (docs/AUTOMATION-SPEC and the class comment: the session being created is recorded as `starting` first and re-created idempotently after `staleStartMs`; reminders are keyed on `turnAt`).

The suggested `stopped` flag would not prevent any user-visible failure. It would mostly add the checks before each side effect that AGENTS.md's "no defensive clutter" rule warns against. Clearing the interval in `stop()` matches how the other services' cleanups in index.server.ts already work.

At most there is a nit: a pass could keep running during the shutdown grace window. It has no impact on users or agents.

rejected.title: open-paseo-plugins AGENTS.md install steps conflict with its own temporary-worktree rule and the git-ref workflow actually used
rejected.why:
The quoted text is at HEAD exactly as cited. open-paseo-plugins/AGENTS.md:10 says to install with `paseo plugin install <插件目录的绝对路径> --id <id>` and then run `paseo plugin reload <id>` after each change. Line 11 says to check that `path` is the tested directory. Line 13 warns against leaving the daemon pointed at a temporary worktree and cites the `kanban` failure ("Plugin manifest is missing"). flowly/docs/verification/automation.md:5 says it followed this file's method, but it actually installed with `paseo plugin install file:///…/flowly --ref sw/flowly-automation` and updated with `paseo plugin update flowly --ref ...`. The memory note flowly-daemon-install.md says the same: the source is a git ref, a git-ref install builds in a checkout Paseo manages so it survives worktree cleanup, and new commits need `plugin update --ref`. So the file only documents the directory install and never mentions the git-ref workflow that was actually used, nor that `reload` is not the right way to update a git-ref install. That gap is real.

Two parts of the finding go too far:
1. Steps 2 and 5 do not really contradict each other. Step 5 lets you test from a temporary worktree and says what to do afterwards (switch back to a stable checkout or the original source, or tell the user). It limits step 2 rather than conflicting with it.
2. The claim that `reload` "does not pick up new commits" for a git install comes only from the memory note. I could not run the paseo CLI to check it.

Scope: the file is in the open-paseo-plugins repo. It is not part of flowly's `git diff 4a332b7..HEAD`, and its last commits (1190e41, 06b2460) are its own. This is a side issue for the workspace's process docs, not a defect in the reviewed branch. Severity stays low: it is documentation only, and step 5 already reduces the risk of a dangling path. | I don't think this is a defect in the reviewed change.

1. **Outside the diff.** The file is open-paseo-plugins/AGENTS.md, in a different repo. It is not among the 66 files in flowly `git diff 4a332b7..HEAD`. Its last commits (06b2460, 1190e41) are the user's own testing-principles docs.

2. **The steps do not contradict each other.** Step 2 (install from a directory, then `reload` after each change) describes the test loop. Step 5 does not ban directory installs from a worktree. It bans leaving the daemon pointed at one "长期" (long-term), and it says what to do when testing ends: switch back to a stable checkout or the original source, or tell the user the daemon points at a temporary path. Step 4 already covers source/remote/revision installs and requires recording how to restore. So an agent that follows steps 2-3 literally from an sw/ worktree is then told by step 5 how to clean up. The `kanban` failure the finding cites happened because that cleanup step was missing, which is why step 5 exists.

3. **The stale-code scenario is caught by an existing rule.** An agent that chose a git-ref install made that choice knowingly; the Flowly verification note records `plugin update --ref` correctly. If it still ran `reload` and saw `running`, step 3 already says `running` proves nothing about features. Web UI rule 2 also requires confirming the just-loaded version (new strings, buttons or version number) before taking screenshots. Stale code would therefore fail verification instead of slipping through.

4. **What remains is an optional improvement, not an error.** The file could mention the git-ref workflow as an alternative that survives worktree cleanup. It could also note that `reload` only re-reads source for directory installs, while git installs need `plugin update --ref`. None of this touches Flowly's product invariants or architecture rules.

5. **The suggested fix goes too far.** Making git-ref the preferred method rewrites the user's documented testing policy in another repo. It is not something to fix as a finding against this branch.

rejected.title: removed/ backups from Delete permanently and Remove project leave out the card's automation job
rejected.why:
The finding holds at HEAD. In BoardStore.deleteTask (server/store.ts:461-505) and removeProject (:360-395), the `removed` object written with writeFile(..., flag "wx") lists tasks, events, agentReceipts, ideas, links, artifacts, workpads and plans. After that, the same mutate callback filters board.automation (lines 503 and 393, both added in this branch's diff). No guard or branch on the way puts the job into the backup, so a card's AutomationJob (state, role, implementerId, reviewerId, reviewRounds, verdict/code, failures, pendingOp) is gone for good. The doc comment on removeProject says the backup exists "so a mistaken removal can be recovered", and earlier specs added each new per-card collection to the backup (CARD-LINKS-SPEC §147 links, CARD-ARTIFACTS-SPEC artifacts, IDEAS-SPEC ideas). This branch breaks that convention. AUTOMATION-SPEC lines 35/88 only say the job is deleted along with the card and say nothing about the backup.

The failure scenario overstates the impact in two ways:
- The user can still tell which sessions were the supervised ones. Automation creates sessions with labels { "flowly-task": task.id, "flowly-automation": role } (server/automation.ts create()), so Paseo itself still marks them as the implementer or reviewer. The task's events, which are in the backup, also record agentId on every turn outcome (note() at :278), on automation_review_approved/changes_requested (:387/:392, the reviewer's id) and on automation_resumed.
- The review loop's history mostly survives: automation_review_started, automation_delivered, automation_failed and automation_retry are all events and so all in the backup.

What is really lost is the job's live snapshot (current state/role, counters, pendingOp, verdict code). That is runtime supervision state. Nothing restores from removed/ automatically, and putting a job back by hand would not restart supervision cleanly anyway.

The attentionDismissals gap existed before this branch (the base 4a332b7 also filters them without backing them up) and they are a display preference, so they are out of scope here.

Net: a real consistency gap in the backup convention, low or very low impact, and the "cannot tell which session" part of the scenario is wrong. | What the finding says is accurate. deleteTask (store.ts ~459-505) and removeProject (~360-395) drop board.automation, and the removed/ backup objects don't include it. The branch's diff to store.ts adds only the two `board.automation = ...filter(...)` lines. attentionDismissals was already missing before this branch: it was added in 7a4562d and is a display preference ("no revision, no Activity"). So that half of the finding is not a regression from this branch.

The claimed impact doesn't hold up:
1. The job is not "the only record of which sessions automation started". Every automation session is created with `labels: { "flowly-task": task.id, "flowly-automation": role }` (automation.ts:522), so Paseo itself can say which session in the workspace was the implementer or the reviewer. The task's events are in the backup, and most automation events carry agentId (turn notes at automation.ts:278, automation_resumed, review verdicts with the reviewer's agentId, the AUTO block move). The review verdict and summary are also in the backed-up events (automation_review_approved / automation_changes_requested, with the note).
2. No code ever reads removed/ back. It is a manual dump. The only real restore path is restoreProject from the project-folder snapshot (project-folder.ts ProjectSnapshot / projectRecords). By design that snapshot also leaves out runtime state: agentReceipts, attentionDismissals and automation. Bringing back a job would be wrong anyway. Its generation, turnAt, pendingOp and implementerId belong to a supervision run that ended when the card was deleted. The spec's way to restart is to queue the card again with "Run with agent", which makes a new job.
3. A job is runtime state for a card that no longer exists. After the delete there is nothing for the dispatcher to resume. That is why it is filtered out next to receipts and dismissals.

So the gap is cosmetic: the dump is a bit less complete, and nothing a user needs is lost. If someone wants the dump to be exhaustive anyway, the fix is harmless and compliant: one more field inside the same serialized mutate, with no client, i18n or polling impact. It is not needed for correctness, and it should not feed any restore path.

rejected.title: A single automation job with an unknown state or code makes the whole board unreadable
rejected.why:
The mechanism is real, but it is the design, not a defect on this branch. At HEAD, BoardStore.load (server/store.ts:68-81) calls upgradeBoard -> storageSchema.parse (server/migrate.ts:66). Any value the schema rejects, anywhere in board.json, throws StoreInvalidError and leaves the file as it is. This matches the AGENTS.md rule "validate input ... preserve invalid data rather than reset it". The whole board model uses strict enums the same way (linkKinds, receipt action, statuses, setup.missing and others), so automation jobs are not a special case.

At HEAD every state and code the daemon writes is in the enum, so the build itself can never produce a value it cannot read. The only trigger is a downgrade (an older build reading a newer file) or a hand edit. The repo does not support downgrades: there is no forward-compat path for any collection.

The reported scenario also fails for a second reason that the suggested fix would not touch. The only place 'waiting'/'sub_cards' is set is the await_children branch (server/automation.ts:305-307), and it runs only when the card has sub-cards. Those sub-cards are stored as links of kind 'subtask', which b35a7c7 added to linkKinds in the same commit. A 7dc715c build would therefore reject the board on board.links whatever automation does. Parsing automation entries one by one would not make the board readable on the older build.

At most this is a general robustness wish (tolerant parsing of runtime-state collections), not a bug this branch introduced. | The mechanism is real: boardSchema.automation is a strict z.array(automationJobSchema), and any parse error makes BoardStore.load throw StoreInvalidError. But it follows the repo's deliberate design, and nobody on a real path hits it.

1) Strict enums plus "preserve invalid data rather than reset it" (AGENTS.md, Architecture) is the rule for the whole board. Statuses, link kinds, artifact roles and kinds, idea and plan statuses and event actors are all z.enum inside the same storageSchema. One bad entry anywhere makes the board unreadable, on purpose: the file is preserved and the user is told to restore a backup. The automation collection is not special. Parsing it per item into "inert records" would add a lenient-parsing path that exists nowhere else in the store, and that is the kind of defensive complexity the rules reject.

2) The failure scenario needs a build no user runs. 'waiting' and 'sub_cards' were added in b35a7c7, but 7dc715c..a6c6a95 are unreleased intermediate commits on the same feature branch (`git branch --contains 7dc715c` shows only sw/flowly-automation, no tag). Downgrading to the base 4a332b7 or to any released build does not trip this check. Those builds have no `automation` key, and zod object strips unknown keys, so the job list is dropped silently. HEAD never writes a state or code outside its own enums, because the TypeScript types restrict them. Pointing the daemon at a mid-branch developer commit to compare behaviour is a developer action, and the recovery the error message gives (restore the file or go back to HEAD) is the designed outcome.

3) A related but different issue is not what this finding claims. This branch also adds linkKinds 'subtask'. Downgrading to the released base after an agent creates a sub-card would hit the strict z.enum(linkKinds) and make the board unreadable. The repo does weigh downgrades in places: PROJECT-FOLDER-SPEC says "so a downgrade keeps working", and TASK-TYPE-SPEC accepts that a downgrade drops types. So that point belongs in a separate, link-level finding, if the user wants downgrades to the released build to survive. It does not support the automation-enum claim as written.

As stated, the finding is harmless in practice and runs against the store's design, so real=false.

rejected.title: Agent-created top-level cards (subCard=false) are auto-queued, so automated agents can spawn unbounded unattended work
rejected.why:
The finding holds at HEAD. I found no other check anywhere that limits this.
- server/agent-service.ts:186-194 queues the new card through `this.automation.queue(task.id, { agentId })` whenever `input.start === "now"` and automation is on for the project. It never looks at `input.subCard`.
- shared/tools.ts:514-516 sets `subCard` to true and `start` to "now" by default.
- `AutomationService.queue` (server/automation.ts:132-160) only checks that the card is not archived, not finished, that the project has automation on, and that no job is already running. It does not check whether the card is a sub-card, who created it, or how many cards agents have created.
- The only limits are `agentCardLimit = 50` per creating card (agent-service.ts:78/154) and `subCardLimits` (depth 3, 20 per parent) in shared/links.ts. Those apply only to sub-card links. A subCard=false card is top-level, so it can create 50 more top-level cards, and so on. Nothing caps the total, and `maxRunning` only limits how many run at once.
- The quoted texts are accurate. SKILL.md line 24 says "create a separate card (subCard=false)". The flowly_propose_idea scope=new description in tool-server.ts:234 says "divergent work (a bug found on the way…)". AGENTS.md line 33 says "Only a card the user queued with Run with agent is started". The 2026-10-22 decision on line 34 only extends that to a parent starting its own direct sub-cards.

One point weakens it. docs/SUB-CARDS-SPEC.md §1 (lines 7-8) explicitly allows independent cards (subCard=false) and says start=now cards are "立即排队" (queued at once) when automation is on, with no exception for top-level cards. So auto-queueing a top-level card follows the user's spec. It is not a slip in the code. It still conflicts with the AGENTS.md invariant, and the lack of any limit on chains of top-level cards appears in neither spec. Changing the queueing rule therefore needs the user's decision. Adding a limit does not conflict with anything.

The risk only exists when the user has turned automation on for a project, and concurrency is still capped. So medium is about right, maybe a little high. | This behaviour is in the spec and was built that way on purpose, so it is not a gap.

1. The spec covers this exact case. docs/SUB-CARDS-SPEC.md §1 says agents may create "独立卡片（subCard=false）" (independent cards). The next bullet says "start=now 放进 Todo，项目开着智能体自动化时立即排队" (start=now puts the card in Todo and queues it right away when the project has automation on). That rule applies to every card an agent creates, not only sub-cards. §3 lists start default "now" for all cards and a result message for the queued case.

2. The user decided this. The spec records the 2026-10-22 decision in the user's words: agents should create cards and sub-cards "像 multica 那样" (like Multica), and "我说怎么做就怎么做" (do it the way I say). In Multica a todo issue starts at once. The AGENTS.md line 34 decision does not limit queuing to a parent starting its sub-cards. Sub-cards with start=now are also queued with no person clicking Run with agent. So the line 33 phrase "Only a card the user queued with Run with agent is started" was already widened by line 34 and the spec for every agent-created card. The finding reads line 33 against a later decision that supersedes it.

3. The commit history says the same. Commit b35a7c7 states "queued when the project runs agent automation" for flowly_create_card with no sub-card condition. The tool description in server/tool-server.ts:363 tells the agent that start=now queues the card when automation is on, and that subCard=false is "for follow-up work that must be done (not just suggested: suggestions stay flowly_propose_idea)".

4. The user's protections still hold. Automation is per project and off by default. A top-level card still never moves to Done or Cancelled without a person (an agent can only accept its own direct sub-cards, so an agent-created top-level card stops in In review). There is a limit of 50 cards per card (CARD_LIMIT), and maxRunning caps how many run at once.

5. The SKILL and the tool text do not really blur ideas and cards. Both say divergent suggestions, such as "a bug found on the way", go to flowly_propose_idea, and work the card needs ("as part of this card or for it") goes to flowly_create_card. An agent would have to misread a stray bug as "must be done" for this to happen.

What the finding gets right: a chain of subCard=false cards is not bounded by the 3-level sub-card depth limit. Each card's agents may create up to 50 more. That is a theoretical runaway risk, but it needs agents to keep misjudging divergent work as required, which is unlikely. Bounding it would be a new policy for the user to choose, not a fix for a bug.

On the suggested fix:
- "Never auto-queue subCard=false cards" or "default start=later for subCard=false" contradicts SUB-CARDS-SPEC §1 and §3 and the user's Multica model.
- A parked subCard=false card cannot be started by its creator: flowly_update_card returns NOT_PARENT for cards that are not its sub-cards. Such cards would sit until a person acts, which quietly changes the agreed design.

If the user wants a guard anyway, they should decide it and record it in SUB-CARDS-SPEC first.

rejected.title: Agent-written text reaches other agents with no provenance (reviewer findings, sub-card descriptions)
rejected.why:
The facts in the finding are mostly accurate, but the conclusion that this is a bug does not hold up.

1) Reviewer half. changesPrompt at shared/automation.ts:257-263 does insert the summary and findings unfenced. But the very first line says where they come from: "[Flowly automation] The reviewer requested changes (review round N of M):". Summary and findings come right after that line, as "- " bullets, then the daemon's "Fix them, rerun the checks…". So the text is not missing its source, and it is not presented as the user's words or as a daemon rule. The design (AUTOMATION-SPEC and the SKILL at server/skill-source.ts:28: "review findings arrive as [Flowly automation] messages; follow them") deliberately has the implementer act on reviewer findings. Telling the implementer to follow a reviewer request is that loop working as designed.

2) Sub-card half. sessionContext (shared/scope.ts:35) does insert task.description raw. createdByAgent (server/service.ts:614) is stored but never put in the context. The finding even overstates the provenance on offer: no non-test code outside agent-service.ts:154 (a count limit) reads createdByAgent, so get_task does not specifically surface it either. The context does include a "Sub-card of: <parent> (<id>) [lane]" line from linkContextLines. Users can also create sub-cards from the UI (client/board.tsx:779 "New sub-card"), so that line does not prove an agent wrote the description. Still, the SKILL (skill-source.ts:24) makes the parent's description the intended carrier of "every decision, file, branch, interface and acceptance criterion". The sub-card agent is supposed to follow it as delegated instructions. Following it is the designed behaviour, not a trust-boundary crossing.

Every party involved (parent agent, reviewer, implementer) is an agent the user launched in their own workspaces, with the same provider permissions. No privilege boundary is crossed, and no code path turns agent text into a user decision. The failure scenario needs an agent that lies or hallucinates ("the user agreed…"), and a provenance line would only partly guard against that. A user-written card description can carry the same text. This is optional prompt hardening (worth considering for sessionContext), not a defect.

I ran a scratch vitest test that called changesPrompt with the scenario's summary. It passed, but the printed output was not captured. The trace above comes from reading the code. I deleted the scratch file afterwards and checked that it was gone. | Both paths work the way the design intends, and both already say where the text came from.

1) changesPrompt (shared/automation.ts:257-263). The first line already names the source: "[Flowly automation] The reviewer requested changes (review round n of m):". So the summary and findings are labelled as the reviewer's, not presented as user or daemon instructions. AUTOMATION-SPEC §5 says the implementer must act on them: "把摘要与发现以 … 发给实现者". SKILL "Automated runs" also says "Reminders, retries and review findings arrive as [Flowly automation] messages; follow them." The reviewer is the user's own configured agent, in the same workspace with the same permissions. It is not an outside party. It is told not to edit, commit, push or change status. The failure scenario ("skip the flaky tests and deliver with acknowledgeOpen") does no real harm. acknowledgeOpen only works with a note that explains every open item. The card stops at In review either way. Done of a top-level card stays a human decision (user decision of 2026-10-22). Fencing the text would add nothing the label does not already give.

2) Sub-card description in sessionContext (shared/scope.ts:35). Putting the parent's text in raw is on purpose. SUB-CARDS-SPEC §3 and SKILL "Cards and sub-cards" require that "its description must carry every decision, file, branch, interface and acceptance criterion it needs; decide shared questions … here once and write them into every card". The sub-card agent is supposed to take those decisions as binding. Its first instructions already carry a "Sub-card of: <parent title> (<id>) [lane]" line (linkContextLines in shared/links.ts, placed before the description). flowly_get_task returns the whole task with createdByAgent. So the context does show that the card belongs to an agent-run parent.

The "push to main" scenario gives a confused parent no new power. The parent agent has the same provider permissions and could push itself. Repo instruction files and provider permissions still bind the sub-card agent. And a sub-card agent that hallucinates is a model-quality problem, not a Flowly defect.

Nobody gains a privilege here and no decision rule is broken, so I am marking this not real.

The suggested fix is harmless but optional. It would be English agent text with no i18n, no daemon write and no polling. If wanted, keep it to one line: in sessionContext, when task.createdByAgent is set, add "Written by the agent of card <parent title> (<id>), not by the user." Wrapping the reviewer text in quotes or code fences is not needed.

rejected.title: Reviewer session has the full write tool set; following the skill's stage rule ends automation
rejected.why:
The code-level fact holds at HEAD. The reviewer is prepared with an ordinary per-card credential. In tool-server.ts every tool is registered for that one identity. AgentService.write (agent-service.ts:588), createCard (:124) and updateCard (:213) never check whether identity.agentId is the job's reviewerId. Only submitReview checks it (automation.ts:363, NOT_REVIEWER). So if a reviewer calls flowly_update_status status=test, the write is accepted: it passes the lane check at :762 and sets task.status = test. automation.cardMoved changes nothing, because test is neither a finished state nor a take-back move. When the reviewer's turn ends, turnDecision (shared/automation.ts:166) returns stop/card_moved and apply() closes the job. No verdict is recorded, the implementer gets no findings, and per spec §6.1 a "stopped" job shows no card signal. That is a real enforcement gap.

The finding overstates how this gets triggered, though:
1. The claim that the skill tells the reviewer to set the stage is refuted. skills/flowly/SKILL.md line 28 (Automated runs) says: "When the instruction says you are the reviewer, review only: never edit files, commit, push or change the card status". reviewPrompt (shared/automation.ts:253) repeats "Do not edit files, commit, push or change the card status". AUTOMATION-SPEC §5 also makes this a prompt-level rule by design. The scenario therefore needs a reviewer model that ignores two explicit instructions, not one that follows the skill.
2. The A1 sub-claim describes a recorded design decision, not a bug. AUTOMATION-SPEC §5 says "活着的评审 session" ("a live reviewer session") is exempt. §8 lists "只有活着的评审者豁免 A1" ("only a live reviewer is exempt from A1") as an acceptance criterion. shared/automation.test.ts:132-137 ("only a live reviewer session is exempt from rule A1") asserts that a delivered job's reviewer is not exempt.
3. Tool restriction would not create a real boundary. The reviewer runs in the same workspace with full file and git access, which is also only prompt-guarded. Accepting the parent's direct sub-cards is within the rights the user granted to the card's agents, and no top-level Done or Cancelled is reachable. The worst outcome is that a misbehaving reviewer ends its own review round and leaves the card in a work stage with no signal.

Net: a low-severity hardening gap (prompt-only role separation), not the medium bug described. | The mechanism is real: the reviewer session gets the same per-card credential as the implementer. AgentService.write, createCard and updateCard never check whether the caller is the job's reviewer. And turnDecision (shared/automation.ts:166) returns stop/card_moved once a reviewer's card is no longer In review. But this is the design the spec chose, not an oversight. AUTOMATION-SPEC §5 sets the reviewer's limits only in the prompt: "只评审，不改文件、不提交、不改卡片状态" (review only, don't edit files, don't commit, don't change the card status). File edits and commits could not be enforced anyway, because the reviewer has a shell.

The finding's premise, that the skill tells the reviewer to set a stage, does not hold up. The skill and the prompt both carve out an exception for reviewers. The skill's "Automated runs" section says: "When the instruction says you are the reviewer, review only: never edit files, commit, push or change the card status, and finish the round with flowly_submit_review". The reviewer's first message (reviewPrompt) repeats "Do not edit files, commit, push or change the card status." A reviewer that still calls flowly_update_status status=test ignores two explicit instructions in its first message, so the scenario is unlikely.

If it does happen, nothing breaks. The card lands in Test, which a person can see and undo. No session is archived or interrupted. The card never goes to Done or Cancelled, and nothing is lost. The same result follows a person moving the card during review (decide("development", reviewer) → card_moved is tested).

Accepting or cancelling the card's own sub-cards would also go against "review only", and nothing in the review prompt invites it.

The A1 point is also deliberate. The test "only a live reviewer session is exempt from rule A1" (shared/automation.test.ts:132) checks that a reviewer session whose job is delivered loses the exemption. Its later turns then fall under the ordinary A1 rule that every Flowly-managed session on the card follows (a user message moves In review to Development). The move is visible and reversible.

Overall this is hardening: a server-side guard would back up a prompt-only rule. It is not a bug against the spec or the user's invariants.

rejected.title: Agent accept/cancel of a sub-card triggers auto wrap-up archiving, contrary to the recorded 'automation never archives sessions'
rejected.why:
The code facts in the finding are correct. index.server.ts:381 sends tools.agents.onStatusChange to afterStatus. When the card enters Done/Cancelled and the autoWrapup pref is on, afterStatus (lines 371-378) calls wrapups.autoArchive. server/agent-service.ts updateCard calls this.onStatusChange after an accept or cancel. So a parent agent's accept or cancel can archive the sub-card's sessions and its worktree workspace.

The claimed contradiction with the docs does not hold up:
- SUB-CARDS-SPEC §4 says this outright: "状态变更以 agent 身份记事件，并触发与人移动卡片相同的后续：停止该卡的自动化 job、释放被它阻塞的卡、自动收尾（设置开启时）、完成卡的项目记忆复盘". In English: an agent's status change has the same follow-ups as a person's move, and that list includes auto wrap-up when the setting is on. §7 also requires the test "移动触发与人相同的后续" (the move triggers the same follow-ups as a person's). This was designed and recorded.
- AGENTS.md line 34 (the sub-cards decision) lets the parent agent accept or cancel its direct sub-cards and points to SUB-CARDS-SPEC for the details.
- AGENTS.md line 39 is the auto wrap-up invariant. It keys on "moving a card into Done/Cancelled" with the user's *Auto wrap up* setting on, the daemon acting "without asking", and only when the preflight is clean. It has no rule about who made the move.
- AGENTS.md line 33 says "It never moves a top-level card to Done or Cancelled and never archives or interrupts sessions". "It" is the agent automation, meaning the dispatcher, supervisor and review loop. Those never archive. AUTOMATION-SPEC agrees (§ Stop automation: "不打断、不归档任何 session", i.e. no session is interrupted or archived), and the automation never moves any card to Done/Cancelled itself.

The archiving in the scenario comes from the separate auto wrap-up feature. It is off by default, the user turns it on, and it then runs on any finish move, whether a person or an agent made it. It is not an automation action. The finding's failure scenario is accurate as a description of behaviour. But it is the documented, intended result of two user decisions (auto wrap-up and agents accepting or cancelling sub-cards). It does not break the "automation never archives" invariant as written. At most AGENTS.md line 34 could cross-reference what SUB-CARDS-SPEC §4 already says. That is a wording nicety, not a mismatch between the docs and the code. | The code path is as described, but the behaviour is intended, documented and opted into. It does not break the recorded decision.

1. **Deliberate and in the spec.** docs/SUB-CARDS-SPEC.md §4 says an agent's accept/cancel "触发与人移动卡片相同的后续：停止该卡的自动化 job、释放被它阻塞的卡、自动收尾（设置开启时）、完成卡的项目记忆复盘". So auto wrap-up is listed by name. The §7 acceptance criteria also require "移动触发与人相同的后续". The same commit (b35a7c7) added the wiring at index.server.ts:380-381, along with a comment that cites §4.

2. **The invariant is about something else.** In AGENTS.md:33, "It never ... archives or interrupts sessions" describes what the automation daemon does by itself: the dispatcher, reminders, retries, the reviewer loop and moves to Blocked. That matches AUTOMATION-SPEC §86/§88: Stop automation and a person's moves do not archive sessions. Accepting or cancelling a sub-card is not a dispatcher action. It is a tool call by the parent card's agent, which AGENTS.md:34 explicitly authorises. The archiving after it comes from AGENTS.md:39: the user's own *Auto wrap up* setting applies to any card entering Done/Cancelled, and the user turns it on by choice. Agent moves of top-level cards to Done/Cancelled stay forbidden. Only direct sub-cards can reach Done/Cancelled this way.

3. **What a user would see.** The setting is off unless the user turns it on. autoArchive (server/wrapup.ts:227) skips when the preflight has any blocker or any warning:
   - a running session blocks it, so nothing is interrupted;
   - uncommitted or local-only commits skip it, so no work is lost;
   - linked or shared workspaces are never archived;
   - the branch is kept, and moving the card out of Done/Cancelled restores the workspace and sessions (WORKSPACE-RESTORE-SPEC).

   A user who turned Auto wrap up on gets exactly that: a finished, clean sub-card is tidied up. That is harmless and expected.

4. **The suggested fix.** Option 1 (an actor flag that skips auto wrap-up for agent moves) is wrong. It contradicts SUB-CARDS-SPEC §4 and the user's opt-in, and it would leave a parent's accepted sub-cards unarchived while the same move by a person would archive them. Option 2 (spell out the exception in AGENTS.md) is fine and harmless, but it only rewords an already consistent rule. It is not a defect fix.

So this is at most an optional wording clarification, not a bug.
